news.title: Football: Soccer-Jamaica rout Costa Rica to secure Women's World Cup berth
news.lede: Nov 27 (Reuters) - Jamaica booked ⁠their place at the 2027 Women's World Cup ⁠with a 3-0 win over Costa Rica in ‌the CONCACAF W Championship quarter-finals on Friday, securing a third consecutive appearance at the global showpiece. The Reggae Girlz took control of the ​match in Mansfield, Texas, from the ⁠outset, with Jody Brown ⁠opening the scoring in the 16th minute with a close-range ⁠finish ‌from a Kalyssa Van Zanten pass. Jamaica doubled their lead in the 59th minute when Van ⁠Zanten finished off a well-worked team move, as ​captain Khadija ‌Shaw, making her 50th international appearance, provided the assist. Manchester ⁠City forward ​Shaw completed the scoring six minutes later with a free kick that took a deflection off the Costa Rica ⁠wall and found the net.

news.title: Morocco reach short-stature football World Cup final with 7-2 win
news.lede: Morocco reached the final of the short-stature football World Cup on home soil on Friday, beating Bolivia 7-2 in the semi-final at the Skikina indoor hall in Temara, near Rabat. The win puts the hosts one game from the title at the second edition of the tournament for players of short stature, the first held in Africa, with 16 national teams taking part, the Moroccan news site Hespress reported. Morocco led 4-0 at half-time after dominating with quick transitions and short passing, and scored three more after the break before Bolivia pulled two goals back late on, Le360 reported. The result was also reported by the regional news agency APA.

news.title: Morocco reach People of Short Stature Football World Cup Final After 7-2 win over Bolivia
news.lede: Morocco’s national people of short stature football team reached the final of the 2026 World Cup after securing a convincing 7-2 victory over Bolivia in their semifinal clash on Friday at Skikina Indoor Sports Hall in Temara. The Moroccan team delivered a strong performance, dominating proceedings and translating its superiority into a five-goal lead before completing the 7-2 victory. The result extended Morocco’s impressive run in the tournament and brought the team one step closer to lifting the trophy on home soil. Morocco had secured its semifinal place with a 3-0 victory over Mexico in Thursday’s quarterfinal, also held at Skikina Indoor Sports Hall in Temara.

news.title: Arab nations discover their round-of-32 opponents at the U-17 World Cup
news.lede: Tough round-of-32 ties await the Arab nations at the U-17 World Cup, as the tournament enters a knockout stage that leaves no room for second chances.All eyes are on Saudi Arabia, who face Belgium after an impressive group stage. They beat France, then booked their place in the knockout rounds with victory over Haiti.Belgium offer another European test, and Saudi Arabia will be determined to extend their run in the tournament.Morocco meet Chile, hoping to keep the Arab presence alive and progress to the next round. Egypt have a tough draw against Colombia. They reached the round of 32 as runners-up in Group A after beating Panama 4-1.

news.title: Threats to withdraw from hosting the 2030 World Cup grow ahead of Spanish election
news.lede: Spain entered the final day of the election campaign ahead of next Sunday's vote, with socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez trying to defy opinion polls that favour the right-wing People's Party. The result won't just matter politically. It could also spill over into football, and specifically the staging of the 2030 World Cup. Alberto Núñez Feijóo, the People's Party candidate for prime minister, has spent several weeks insisting that Spain, co-hosts of the next World Cup alongside Portugal and Morocco, would have no choice but to pull out of the hosting bid if they aren't awarded the final.

news.title: Sasol Banyana eyeing positive start in World Cup play-offs
news.lede: 27 November 2026 – Sasol Banyana Banyana are looking to get a positive start in their opening match of the FIFA Women’s World Cup Inter-Continental Play-offs when they come up against Chinese Taipei at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat on Saturday. Kickoff is at 16h00 SA Time. The two nations are part of the six taking part in the mini-tournament in Morocco, with the main aim of being among the top two to advance to the final qualification stage in February next year. South Africa and Chinese Taipei will be meeting for the first time, bringing together contrasting styles of play.
